stem: Calculate the energy released in the nuclear reaction: $^1_0n + ^{235}_{92}U \\rightarrow ^{141}_{56}Ba + ^{92}_{36}Kr + 3^1_0n + Q$. Given the following masses: Mass of uranium-235: 235.12142 u, Mass of barium-141: 140.883 u, Mass of krypton-92: 91.9262 u, Mass of neutron: 1.008665 u. Use the conversion factor 1 u = 931.5 MeV/c².
solution_latex:
Total mass on L.H.S = Mass of neutron + Mass of U-235 = $1.008665 \text{ u} + 235.12142 \text{ u} = 236.1301 \text{ u}$
Total mass on R.H.S = Mass of Ba-141 + Mass of Kr-92 + 3 * Mass of neutron = $140.883 \text{ u} + 91.9262 \text{ u} + (3 \times 1.008665) \text{ u} = 140.883 \text{ u} + 91.9262 \text{ u} + 3.025995 \text{ u} = 235.835195 \text{ u}$
Energy released Q = (Total mass on L.H.S - Total mass on R.H.S) * 931.5 MeV/u
Q = $(236.1301 \text{ u} - 235.835195 \text{ u}) \times 931.5 \text{ MeV/u}$
Q = $0.294905 \text{ u} \times 931.5 \text{ MeV/u}$
Q = $274.699 \text{ MeV}$ (approximately)
Note: The context provides the calculation in MeV/c², but the question asks for energy. Assuming the conversion to MeV is implied.
